A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with matching core methods, proofs and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MimicGen experiments, component ablations, real-robot evaluations and a pretraining study in Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 retains the original simulation and robot results and reports additional pretraining, perturbation, action-control and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The principal policy remains unchanged and is renamed ISP. Appendix G adds an experimental variant that removes rotation correction and predicts gripper-relative delta actions, a limited procedural adaptation. The newly documented learnable projection does not independently establish that the original implementation changed.

E1.justification: The twelve MimicGen tasks, ImageNet-1k pretraining and four real-world tasks are retained. V3 adds distinct visual conditions on Box-Pipe Disassembly: changed lighting, background clutter and temporary camera occlusion. Its expanded pretraining study reuses tasks already evaluated elsewhere in v1.

E2.justification: The main Diffusion Policy, modified EquiDiff and ACT comparisons are retained. However, v1's pretraining study compares both ISP and Diffusion Policy with and without pretraining, whereas v3 Table 3 drops Diffusion Policy from that comparison. V3 Table 6 additionally evaluates delta-control Diffusion Policy.

E3.justification: The established training and evaluation settings are retained. New protocols compare absolute and delta control on two tasks with 100 demonstrations, evaluate perturbations over 20 rollouts with matched initial states, and measure efficiency using 16-step DDIM on an RTX 4090. The 60 evaluations and fixed rollout set are newly disclosed details, not established changes to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: V3 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through the action-frame/rotation-correction study, real-world visual perturbation tests and computational-efficiency analysis. The pretraining analysis expands from five to twelve tasks, while its learning curves and comparison with Diffusion Policy are removed. The original component ablations and task-specific failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix E and Table 4 label the uncertainty as standard error, despite standard-deviation wording in the main text. V3 Appendix F and Table 5 label the retained values as standard deviations, with some equivalent rounding. V3 also specifies seed identities 0, 1 and 2; both versions use three runs, with no reported increase.

E6.justification: The principal simulation, component-ablation and real-world success rates are unchanged. V3 adds seven pretraining-task entries, reporting 72.1% versus 65.0% across twelve tasks; the five overlapping tasks retain their scores. New results include ISP delta-control success rates of 22% and 57%, perturbation rates of 85%, 75% and 85%, and inference times of 68/63/75 ms for DiffPo/ISP-SO(2)/ISP-SO(3). V1's Diffusion Policy pretraining results and learning curves are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, two propositions, equations and subgroup-equivariance argument are retained. V1 Appendix A's spectral proof moves to v3 Appendix B without substantive alteration. Clarified prose about inverse camera rotation and new conceptual discussions do not introduce a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the first monocular-RGB SO(3)-equivariant policy claim, global-equivariance/local-invariance claims, and performance and sample-efficiency contributions. The stated 11.6% simulation and 42.5% real-world improvements remain unchanged. Naming the method ISP does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Beyond the retained limitations, v3 discusses camera-intrinsic sensitivity, gravity and joint-limit asymmetries, and finite-subgroup approximation in Appendices A and L. It adds interpretations concerning sensor integration, control frames and imperfect transfer from pretraining. Some new interpretation overreaches: Appendix G says absolute control consistently wins, although Table 6 reports DiffPo at 14% with delta versus 12% with absolute control on Square D2.

D1.justification: V3 substantially expands documentation with HEALPix sampling and learned feature aggregation for projection, evaluation frequency and checkpoint-selection details, and practical demonstration collection and pruning guidance. It also identifies the GPU and sampling configuration for timing measurements and adds a project-page link. These disclosures do not establish that the earlier implementation or data processing was changed.

R1.justification: V3 retains the earlier references and adds works including SEIL, Fourier Transporter, affine-equivariant networks, latent-symmetry research, ResNet and U-Net. Related-work positioning remains centered on monocular eye-in-hand equivariance, with limited revisions emphasizing integration with other frameworks and removing the earlier broad computational-cost criticism of competing architectures.

P1.justification: V3 introduces consistent ISP terminology, edits the introduction, related work and symmetry explanation, and moves the pretraining discussion from Appendix F into Section 5.1. Appendix headings, affiliations and acknowledgments are updated. The main section sequence and much of the existing exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The empirical presentation is substantially reworked: v1's pretraining learning curves disappear, and its five-task, four-method table becomes a twelve-task, two-method table in the main text. V3 adds the perturbation photographs and control/efficiency tables, redraws Figure 3 and relocates Figure 2. Most existing task illustrations and core result-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves assessability through clearer projection and evaluation documentation, quantified computational costs, additional diagnostics and more substantive applicability limits. These gains are moderated by removing the Diffusion Policy pretraining comparison and learning curves. The perturbation study also compares perturbed ISP-SO(2) with an unperturbed ISP-SO(3) reference, and the control interpretation has a Table 6 exception. Overall, the retained central evidence is better documented and supplemented, but the new analyses have limitations that constrain the improvement.
